deckTitle: Beyond the Banalities of Good vs Evil — Uncle FrizzleBob's KAYFABIZARRO Komik Kards for Monster Morality Wrestling & Flexible Kayfabizarro Ethiks
seriesContext: Filename prefix "KAYFABIZARRO-1" implies Vol. 1 of a series. No companion volumes visible in this upload. Pair candidate: Narrow Path / Wide Road ethics decks.

cards.power: Steal audience sympathy while doing the exact same job as the villain.
cards.lore: You're just a Complete Monster with a better PR team and a highly marketable tragic backstory.
cards.gradeReason: "Doing the exact same job as the villain" lands the satire in the POWER itself — no LORE required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with purple watercolor wash. Subject: Leather-jacketed badger balanced on tightrope between hero cape and villain mask. Mood: Smug and effortlessly on-brand.

cards.power: Absorb all audience hatred to instantly shield the writers from having to write nuance.
cards.lore: A narrative shortcut for lazy authors who need you to stop thinking and start blindly booing.
cards.gradeReason: "Shield the writers from having to write nuance" is a satirical knife that lands the moment you read it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Snarling hyena holding a lit bomb, foam finger vendor looking on. Mood: Mindlessly, efficiently menacing.

cards.power: Annoy the entire roster into compliance through weaponized purity.
cards.lore: Adherence to the rules so absolute it becomes a form of psychological warfare against the audience.
cards.gradeReason: "Weaponized purity" is a two-word satirical compression that immediately generates the recognition moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Pristine white poodle radiating blinding light, others shielding their eyes. Mood: Aggressively, exhaustingly innocent.

cards.power: Justify extreme, horrific violence by pointing at your shiny 'Good Guy' badge.
cards.lore: You think you're the hero, but your extremist methods are just villainy with a righteous paint job.
cards.gradeReason: "Pointing at your shiny 'Good Guy' badge" is performative and immediate — the gesture IS the character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with red splatter. Subject: Armored rooster assaulting a cowering turtle, Templar cross gleaming. Mood: Righteously, unambiguously brutal.

cards.power: Extract maximum audience tension by refusing to do your job until the last possible second.
cards.lore: You're scared to death, but the script demands you accidentally do the right thing eventually.
cards.gradeReason: "Accidentally do the right thing eventually" makes the satirical point; player knows exactly what procrastination to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Massive sweating bear trembling in front of a single folding chair. Mood: Dramatically, uselessly terrified.

cards.power: Hijack the narrative's moral high ground while maintaining entirely selfish motivations.
cards.lore: You are considered a hero not because it's right, but because it aligns with your personal grift.
cards.gradeReason: "Personal grift" is the satirical payload; the POWER delivers it cleanly without needing the LORE.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with gold watercolor. Subject: Raccoon clutching oversized "Hero of the Year" trophy, bills raining from hidden pocket. Mood: Self-congratulatory and quietly corrupt.

cards.power: Immune to moral criticism. Reality warps to justify your actions.
cards.lore: "I am on the right side, therefore anything I do to you is mathematically incapable of being wrong."
cards.gradeReason: LORE is the strongest direct-quote POWER in the deck; the quoted logic IS the satirical exposure, verbatim.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with fire background. Subject: Armored lion holding a mirror that reflects a serene angel while flames rise behind it. Mood: Completely, contentedly self-deceived.

cards.power: Bypass all Moral Dilemma cards. Empathy is a mechanic for weaker players.
cards.lore: Incapable of feeling compassion, leaving you completely unburdened by the pesky rules of the kayfabe.
cards.gradeReason: "Empathy is a mechanic for weaker players" is the deck's best single-sentence satirical punchline — embedded directly in the POWER.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Iguana sipping boba through a straw while two rodents battle explosively behind it. Mood: Profoundly, constitutionally unbothered.

cards.power: Instantly trigger the "Protect the Mascot" objective for all nearby players.
cards.lore: You have absolutely no traces of evil in you, making you an incredibly boring liability to the team.
cards.gradeReason: The satirical punch lives entirely in LORE — "incredibly boring liability" — while the POWER reads as a game trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Radiant lamb hovering in divine light above two overwhelmed wrestlers on their knees. Mood: Transcendently, punishingly dull.

cards.power: Confuse the audience into rooting against the actual heroes.
cards.lore: You're a villain who forgot to pack traditional evil qualities, relying entirely on aesthetic brooding.
cards.gradeReason: "Forgot to pack traditional evil qualities" lands the satirical beat cleanly and immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with rain. Subject: Weeping wolf in a dramatic cape carefully constructing a birdhouse in a thunderstorm. Mood: Ostentatiously, fashionably tragic.

cards.power: Paralyze your tag-team partner with weaponized guilt.
cards.lore: The designated character whose sole job is to act as an un-ignorable, highly annoying moral guideline.
cards.gradeReason: "Weaponized guilt" is a precise satirical compound that lands before the LORE even arrives.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Tiny grasshopper with megaphone confronting a bewildered, paralyzed hippo. Mood: Insufferably, righteously relentless.

cards.power: Generate infinite sin tokens to bribe the referee.
cards.lore: You don't just do immoral acts; you are the merchandising rights for immorality itself.
cards.gradeReason: "Merchandising rights for immorality itself" is the real punchline but it lives in LORE — POWER is a funny mechanic, not yet the exposure.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with lurid color wash. Subject: Tattooed pig luxuriating in a bathtub overflowing with sin tokens, tentacles everywhere. Mood: Cheerfully, professionally depraved.

cards.power: Convert all your collected "Prayers" into "Spite" tokens.
cards.lore: Losing your belief in the universe's booking committee instantly transforms you into a top-tier villain.
cards.gradeReason: The token conversion requires knowing what "Prayers" and "Spite" tokens mean; punchline needs LORE context to fully arrive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Armored sheep mid-transformation, shredding white wedding robes to reveal spiked black armor. Mood: Gleefully, irreversibly betrayed.

cards.power: Disarm an opponent by forcing a mandatory hug sequence.
cards.lore: The naive belief that a systemic apex predator wouldn't be so evil if they just had a buddy.
cards.gradeReason: "Mandatory hug sequence" is a physically specific satirical image that generates the laugh before you finish the sentence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Blood-soaked tiger and terrified antelope in an extremely awkward mandatory embrace. Mood: Desperately, structurally naive.

cards.power: Bypass faction-specific traps by pretending you belong there.
cards.lore: You betray your own people by refusing to stick to the demographic the marketing team assigned you.
cards.gradeReason: "The demographic the marketing team assigned you" is the satirical knife, and it lives in LORE — POWER alone is just tactical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor. Subject: Penguin in crudely attached shark fins paddling nervously through a shark formation. Mood: Tensely, unconvincingly assimilated.

cards.power: Farm unlimited pity from the audience for crimes you already enjoyed committing.
cards.lore: A character seeking to make up for bad deeds, mostly because the consequences finally caught up.
cards.gradeReason: "Crimes you already enjoyed committing" is embedded in the POWER and is the exact satirical point — no interpretation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with grey wash. Subject: Battered gorilla taking a theatrical bow amid debris and still-smoking victims. Mood: Performatively, belatedly remorseful.

cards.power: Inherit the stats of a dead villain without the moral baggage.
cards.lore: Taking an identity previously used for evil and slapping a fresh coat of "Good" PR on it.
cards.gradeReason: "Inherit the stats without the moral baggage" is an immediately recognizable narrative critique that lands as both funny and exact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Cheerful golden retriever proudly wearing a blood-spattered villain's spiked mask, tail wagging. Mood: Blithely, brightly inheriting evil.

cards.power: Gain villain abilities, but lose your hero insurance.
cards.lore: You fought the evil so hard, you accidentally memorized their playbook and started using it.
cards.gradeReason: "Hero insurance" is a satirical coinage precise enough to generate instant recognition — it earns its G1 on three syllables.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Caped goat staring into a cracked mirror that shows a horned demon staring back. Mood: Dawning, unavoidable horror.

cards.power: Permanently lock your alignment to "Unforgivable."
cards.lore: You've done too much wrong to ever be forgiven. Welcome to the permanent Heel roster.
cards.gradeReason: "Welcome to the permanent Heel roster" translates the moral-philosophy concept into wrestling terminology with perfect FrizzleBob register.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Fox striding forward on a red carpet, its shadow solidifying into a solid black monster behind it. Mood: Resigned to permanent damnation.

cards.power: Deal double damage during a cooperative tag-team maneuver.
cards.lore: They claim to be your tag partner, but they are just waiting for the referee to look away.
cards.gradeReason: POWER reads as a pure game mechanic; the satirical exposure of treachery lives entirely in the LORE.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Large brown bear beaming in an embrace with a smaller black bear, scissors raised behind partner's back. Mood: Warmly, professionally murderous.

cards.power: Automatically fail any redemption arc to retain your cool aesthetic.
cards.lore: You can never be free of being evil. The universe literally bends to make your hobbies malicious.
cards.gradeReason: "Fail any redemption arc to retain your cool aesthetic" is a precise satirical observation about narrative economics built into the POWER.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Enormous cobra serenely knitting while a tiny mouse watches in frozen terror. Mood: Unavoidably, aesthetically evil.

cards.power: Intercept all incoming damage directed at NPCs, whether you want to or not.
cards.lore: You can never abandon somebody in need, making you the easiest mark in the arena.
cards.gradeReason: "Whether you want to or not" flips the heroism into compulsion — that four-word satirical inversion is the whole card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with action lines. Subject: Bleeding war horse charging into explosions toward a runaway baby carriage, expression resigned. Mood: Compulsively, catastrophically heroic.

cards.power: Gain a massive surprise attack bonus against both factions.
cards.lore: You finally choose a side after realizing the audience was falling asleep.
cards.gradeReason: "The audience was falling asleep" is the satirical punchline but it lives in LORE — POWER alone is a straight tactical mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Sloth half-awake in a hammock, casually leveling a massive rocket launcher at both sides of the arena. Mood: Bored menace finally activated.

cards.power: Immune to all 'Reveal Traitor' mechanics.
cards.lore: Everyone suspects you of being a mastermind, but the horrifying truth is you are exactly as boring as you seem.
cards.gradeReason: The satirical punchline — "horrifyingly, you are exactly as boring as you seem" — lives in LORE; POWER is a mechanic immunity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Perfectly ordinary sheep under a harsh interrogation lamp, refusing categorically to be interesting. Mood: Anticlimactically, disappointingly innocent.

cards.power: Force all gray-area characters to pick a side or take fatal damage.
cards.lore: An extremely binary moral worldview where anyone slightly disagreeing with you is one-dimensionally evil.
cards.gradeReason: LORE explains the concept; POWER is a strong mechanic but doesn't deliver the satirical recognition on its own.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Owl referee painting half the ring pure black and half pure white with a giant roller. Mood: Authoritarian, cheerfully intolerant of nuance.

cards.power: Your actions become completely immune to standard logic checks.
cards.lore: Morality that's so bizarre, unconventional, and distorted that the referee's brain melts trying to score it.
cards.gradeReason: "The referee's brain melts trying to score it" makes the exposure immediate and visual — no translation required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Psychedelic watercolor. Subject: Kaleidoscopic octopus surrounded by floating geometric shapes, top-hatted and serene. Mood: Dizzying, self-consistent alien logic.

cards.power: Automatically resurrect the villain if the hero wins too decisively.
cards.lore: Good and evil must exist in balance, which gives the worst villains endless loopholes to make a grand return.
cards.gradeReason: The POWER is a strong mechanic-as-satire; LORE adds "endless loopholes" but doesn't sharpen to a punchline.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Two hands holding a scale — one side a tiny caped hero, other side a tiny villain, referee annotating a spreadsheet. Mood: Cosmically, profitably rigged.

cards.power: Generate profit by keeping the central conflict completely unresolved.
cards.lore: Without a heel to fight, the hero loses their merchandising deal. Evil is just job security.
cards.gradeReason: "Evil is just job security" is a four-word satirical compression that closes the card perfectly and immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Eagle in superhero cape reviewing a villain's itemized services invoice, nodding seriously. Mood: Institutionally, transparently corrupt.

cards.power: Extract resources from heroic players who think they are saving the world.
cards.lore: Heroic groups are secretly being managed by the exact villains they are trying to punch.
cards.gradeReason: "The exact villains they are trying to punch" is the satirical point delivered cleanly — the structure IS the joke.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Suited rats operating hidden gears and levers beneath a sunlit heroic castle. Mood: Conspiratorial, entirely unsurprising.

cards.power: Rewrite one rule on the board mid-game purely out of spite.
cards.lore: The traditionally good, all-knowing force actually hates you and is booking this match for laughs.
cards.gradeReason: "Booking this match for laughs" is a perfect FrizzleBob line — the cosmic figure reframed as a bored matchmaker.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with glowing red eyes. Subject: Massive tentacled shadow creature grinning as it operates puppet strings above a wrestling ring. Mood: Cosmically, casually malevolent.

cards.power: Drain all passion and kinetic energy from the current turn.
cards.lore: An extremely middle-ground worldview positing that everyone's on the same morally dubious, boring level.
cards.gradeReason: Both POWER and LORE describe the concept academically — neither generates the satirical recognition moment the card name promises.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with grey wash. Subject: Two featureless grey figures exchanging identical documents in a completely empty room. Mood: Terminally, symmetrically noncommittal.

cards.power: Any war crime you commit is automatically reclassified as a "quirky mistake."
cards.lore: You're the protagonist, therefore anyone not explicitly clapping for you must be an enemy.
cards.gradeReason: "War crime → quirky mistake" is the cleanest satirical compression in the entire deck. Both lines are G1 on their own.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Beaming dog in superhero cape looking noble while the city burns cheerfully behind it. Mood: Blissfully, architecturally oblivious.

cards.power: Destroy the current arena, removing all rules for one turn.
cards.lore: The establishment's propaganda that any deviation from their script is a force for ultimate villainy.
cards.gradeReason: The political punch lives in LORE — "establishment's propaganda" is the exposure. POWER alone is an arena mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with action lines. Subject: Furniture-filled chaos tornado consuming a wrestling ring while an owl referee dives for cover. Mood: Liberatingly, terrifyingly rule-free.

cards.power: Paralyze an opponent with insurmountable bureaucratic red tape.
cards.lore: Tradition and rules aren't here to protect you; they're here to make sure you stay in your cubicle.
cards.gradeReason: "Stay in your cubicle" is the satirical payoff but it lives in LORE — POWER is a strong mechanic image, not yet the exposure.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Thousands of bees arranged in perfect grid formation, every cell identical. Mood: Oppressively, architecturally compliant.

cards.power: Ignore all moral-based attacks because you simply "do not care."
cards.lore: You aren't really concerned with good or evil. You just want everyone to know you're smarter than them.
cards.gradeReason: "You just want everyone to know you're smarter than them" is a perfect deflation of Nietzschean posturing — arrives with the clarity of a fact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Elegant flamingo reading a philosophy book beside a cheerful mushroom cloud, expression serene. Mood: Serenely, constitutionally superior.

cards.cardName: Sliding Scale of Idealism vs. Cynicism
cards.power: Flip the game's tone: positive effects become negative, and vice versa.
cards.lore: Optimism and pessimism locked in an eternal, agonizing grappling match.
cards.gradeReason: LORE is a generic description — "eternal agonizing grappling match" could describe any abstract conflict — and delivers no recognition moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Puppy with a rainbow balloon and a vulture with a newspaper balanced on a catastrophically tilting seesaw. Mood: Inevitably, structurally unstable.

cards.power: Generate instant, massive heat from the audience to establish yourself as the Heel.
cards.lore: A gratuitously cruel act used when the writer is too lazy to give you actual character development.
cards.gradeReason: "Too lazy to give you actual character development" lands as both exact analysis and punchline — the card is doing media criticism in two lines.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Vulture mid-swing with a folding chair, tiny puppy airborne, audience outraged. Mood: Gratuitously, efficiently villainous.

cards.power: Eliminate a sympathetic character to force the plot forward.
cards.lore: You're forced to do something horrible for the "greater good," but mostly for the drama.
cards.gradeReason: "But mostly for the drama" is a perfect satirical addendum that undercuts the moral justification in four words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Weeping deer reluctantly aiming a rocket launcher at a small glowing evil puppy. Mood: Tortured, transparent, and mostly dramatic.

cards.power: Steal an item from another player and successfully argue why it's fair.
cards.lore: You have a perfectly logical, highly detailed reason for committing blatant theft.
cards.gradeReason: POWER and LORE state the same observation twice without adding satirical sharpness; card name carries more weight than either line.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Raccoon at whiteboard presenting an elaborate multi-step theft justification to a skeptical-looking dog. Mood: Elaborately, transparently rationalized.

cards.power: Cancel any incoming punishment by paying double its value in tokens.
cards.lore: Avoiding owning up to your misdeeds through the ultimate superpower: liquid capital.
cards.gradeReason: "The ultimate superpower: liquid capital" is the satirical punch but it lives in LORE — POWER is a token exchange mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Suited cat cramming money into a zebra referee's pocket, crowd looking away strategically. Mood: Casually, institutionally corrupt.

cards.power: Sacrifice a low-tier friendly unit to survive a board-wipe.
cards.lore: Sacrificing one life to save others, usually while looking incredibly brooding and sad about it.
cards.gradeReason: "Usually while looking incredibly brooding and sad about it" is a satirical observation embedded in the LORE that confirms and completes the POWER's satirical intent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with grey wash. Subject: Walrus in captain's hat gravely pushing a penguin from an overloaded lifeboat, expression correctly tragic. Mood: Brooding, mathematically necessary.

cards.power: Deal 10x damage in response to being poked.
cards.lore: Harsh, apocalyptic vengeance for the most petty, mundane slights imaginable.
cards.gradeReason: "10x damage in response to being poked" is the joke — the ratio between trigger and response IS the satirical payload.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with explosion. Subject: Enormous elephant deploying a nuclear bomb in response to a single mosquito bite, ants watching. Mood: Cosmically, proportionally catastrophic.

cards.power: Use villain weapons without taking an alignment penalty.
cards.lore: Doing horrific, mean things is totally justified if the victim was a jerk first.
cards.gradeReason: "The victim was a jerk first" reduces a millennia-old ethical debate to a playground logic that lands as both funny and exact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Squirrel with a halo gleefully swinging a barbed baseball bat. Mood: Righteously, cheerfully violent.

cards.power: Sacrifice your tag-team partner to instantly escape the arena.
cards.lore: You'll leave everyone else to die to save your own butt, and you won't even feel bad about it.
cards.gradeReason: "You won't even feel bad about it" is the satirical precision — the absence of guilt is the point, and it's right there in the LORE.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with speed lines. Subject: Cheetah sprinting away from a falling anvil aimed at an oblivious tortoise. Mood: Shamelessly, aerodynamically self-preserving.

cards.power: Keep an opponent alive but completely remove their ability to play the game.
cards.lore: Letting your enemy live with a Fate Worse Than Death so you can keep your "Hero" rating.
cards.gradeReason: "So you can keep your 'Hero' rating" is the satirical exposure — the LORE reveals the merciful act as a reputation management strategy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Grinning lion holding a terrified dog inside a tiny locked car, receiving a Good Samaritan certificate. Mood: Magnanimously, calculatingly monstrous.

cards.power: Force an opponent's card to permanently fight for you.
cards.lore: Stripping away free will is perfectly acceptable as long as it's for a "good cause."
cards.gradeReason: The quotation marks around "good cause" do the satirical work quietly and precisely — the entire political tradition is indicted in two words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with neon rings. Subject: Owl with hypnotic glowing rings converting snarling wolves into smiling, compliant sheep. Mood: Serenely, efficiently totalitarian.

cards.cardName: Get Out of Jail Free Card
cards.power: Automatically cancel any "Arrest" or "Banish" effect.
cards.lore: You cut the villain a break because they are too popular with the fanbase to write out of the story.
cards.gradeReason: LORE names the meta-narrative excuse sharply, but POWER is a pure game mechanic without embedded satirical payload.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Bulldog in barrister wig brandishing an oversized Monopoly card at a stunned judge. Mood: Unapologetically, precedentally above the law.

cards.power: Ignore all puzzle mechanics and just destroy the target.
cards.lore: When moral dilemmas and negotiations get too complicated, just use the easy way out.
cards.gradeReason: LORE restates POWER without adding any satirical angle — the card name outperforms both lines combined.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: A massive red "JUST KILL EM" stamp obliterating a fifteen-step diplomatic flowchart. Mood: Impatiently, definitively final.

cards.power: Evade all end-of-game consequences regardless of your alignment score.
cards.lore: You get away scot-free with everything, infuriating the audience and breaking the cosmic scales.
cards.gradeReason: "Infuriating the audience and breaking the cosmic scales" is a double satirical payload — the moral AND the audience-contract violation in one line.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Smiling snake dodging a cascade of falling anvils and grand pianos with zero effort. Mood: Infuriatingly, cosmically untouchable.

cards.power: Defeat an opponent by letting them trigger their own trap.
cards.lore: The universe finally remembers to do its job, and you die as a direct, ironic consequence of your wickedness.
cards.gradeReason: "The universe finally remembers to do its job" is a perfect FrizzleBob line — the satire is in the belated, reluctant competence of cosmic justice.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with purple wash. Subject: Pelican mid-air, coins spilling, struck by a bolt of ironic karmic lightning it clearly earned. Mood: Cosmically overdue, narratively satisfying.

cards.power: Claim victory, but your character is permanently retired.
cards.lore: After enduring absolute hell, everything works out for you... assuming you survive the trauma.
cards.gradeReason: The ellipsis before "assuming you survive the trauma" is a precision beat — FrizzleBob timing at its best.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Bandaged rabbit giving a thumbs-up atop a mountain of defeated enemies, expression exhausted. Mood: Triumphant, technically, if barely.

cards.power: Take 2 damage every time you use a "Heal" or "Protect" action.
cards.lore: Doing good deeds actively backfires, proving the kayfabe is rigged against the pure.
cards.gradeReason: POWER implements the saying mechanically; LORE names the concept without sharpening it — the card name is still the strongest line.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Cheerful beaver presenting a completed dam, immediately handed a tower of violation notices by a bureaucrat pig. Mood: Cosmically, reliably penalized.

cards.cardName: Screw the Rules, I Have Money!
cards.power: Ignore any game rule by paying the bank.
cards.lore: Being rich lets you buy a private, luxury box outside of the morality spectrum.
cards.gradeReason: "A private, luxury box outside of the morality spectrum" is an image precise enough to generate the recognition moment without requiring additional context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with gold. Subject: Top-hatted alligator in velvet chair channeling stacks of money into reality-warping laser beams. Mood: Gleefully, transparently above the law.

cards.power: Gain massive end-game points for a completely trivial action.
cards.lore: Being rewarded excessively for a minor act of kindness, throwing the entire economy out of balance.
cards.gradeReason: Both lines describe the concept without delivering a satirical punch — LORE adds "entire economy" but doesn't generate the recognition moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink. Subject: Lion in full royal regalia solemnly placing a golden crown on a bewildered pigeon. Mood: Absurdly, economically consequential.

cards.power: Convert all stored 'Good Karma' directly into win conditions.
cards.lore: You did the bare minimum of good deeds, and the universe decides to pay out the jackpot.
cards.gradeReason: "The bare minimum of good deeds" is the satirical precision — it quantifies the moral performance at exactly the right level of mediocrity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with gold wash. Subject: Halo-wearing golden retriever hitting a jackpot slot machine, coins exploding everywhere. Mood: Effortlessly, disproportionately blessed.

cards.power: Instantly delete one specific opponent who has wronged you.
cards.lore: After 10 seasons of getting away with it, the writers finally remember you exist and drop the hammer.
cards.gradeReason: "The writers finally remember you exist" is a perfect meta-narrative exposure — specific, late, and exactly right.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink with fire trail. Subject: Cockroach in dramatic cape fleeing a precisely targeted flaming smiley-face comet. Mood: Inevitably, specifically doomed.

verdict: This is one of the tightest decks in the corpus — G3 count of 3/56 (5%) is unusually low and reflects genuine copywriting discipline rather than easy grading. The satirical arc is structurally complete: you can read the section headers alone and get the entire moral-trope taxonomy. Weaknesses are local: three LORE fields describe their concept instead of landing it (Grey-and-Gray Insanity, Sliding Scale, Murder Is the Best Solution), and the "Conceptual Heavyweights" section is one notch below the rest in POWER sharpness. Fix: give those three LORE fields the same treatment as "evil is just job security" — compress to a single satirical sentence that lands before it finishes. Table-ready: Y.
blurb: 56 cards that give every moral trope in fiction its own wrestling persona — from Tautological Templar to Karma Houdini. Play it when the story needs a villain who genuinely believes they're right.

qa.readability: 9 — Large type, 2×2 grid is visually consistent throughout; background textures occasionally reduce contrast on pages 8–9 but no legibility failures.
qa.artworkConsistency: 8 — Ink-with-watercolor style holds across all 14 content pages; background treatment shifts between pipe-industrial and clean cream, which creates mild tonal discord but no identity inconsistency.
qa.comedyTiming: 9 — POWER/LORE beat structure is consistently well-timed; most cards deliver the setup in POWER and the satirical knife in LORE. "Empathy is a mechanic for weaker players," "evil is just job security," and "war crime → quirky mistake" are corpus-level punchlines.
qa.satiricalCoherence: 9 — The arc from character archetypes → face/heel turns → systemic illusions → dirty moves → karmic payout is a structurally coherent satirical anatomy of moral storytelling. Each section earns its place.
qa.frizzleBobVoice: 8 — The majority of LORE fields are in genuine FrizzleBob register. Three cards (Grey-and-Gray Insanity, Sliding Scale of Idealism vs. Cynicism, Murder Is the Best Solution) drift into straight description, and a handful of LORE fields run a beat too long. The POWER fields are tighter than the LOREs on average.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — FrizzleBob (yellow cartoon rabbit) center-ring, wielding a chair stacked with Aristotle/Kant/Nietzsche books, wrestling ring with balance scales, lightning bolts, peripheral characters. Energetic and immediately characterful; slight weakness is that dense composition loses legibility at thumbnail scale.
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — "Beyond the Banalities of Good vs Evil" is punchy, immediately signals the satirical register, and the subtitle delivers the product promise without academic drag. Corpus-best title work.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Wrestling ring, philosophy chair-smash, ethics scales — the cover IS the deck. No bait-and-switch.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — The philosophy-wrestling mashup is the deck's genuine concept and the cover executes it with style; slightly conventional in the "everything on one cover" compositional approach.
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Strong scroll-stop energy at full size; busy composition may need a second read at thumbnail, which slightly reduces cold-scroll impact.
coverQA.coverNote: The cover earns its energy — FrizzleBob as the unhinged referee of a morality wrestling match is the right visual thesis statement for this deck. The compositional density is both the cover's strength (nothing is missing) and its only liability (nothing has room to breathe). For future editions: consider isolating FrizzleBob + scales + one antagonist as a cleaner thumbnail crop.
